course.department: Department of Urban and Regional Planning

content.value: Let L is a point on the line $\textstyle { \frac { x - 2 } { 3 } } = { \frac { y - 3 } { 4 } } = { \frac { z - 4 } { 5 } }$ and M be on the line $\textstyle { \frac { x - 2 } { 0 } } = { \frac { y - 5 } { 3 } } = { \frac { z + 1 } { - 2 } }$ such that LM denotes the shortest distance between the lines. Find the coordinates of L and M and hence obtain the equations of the line of shortest distance.

_source_title: B.Sc. Engineering 1st Year 1st Term Regular Examination, 2015
